The patient reports that the cough and shortness of breath have persisted for one month, worsening with exertion and at night, following a recent upper respiratory infection eight weeks ago. She denies waking up gasping for air but notes that the symptoms are impacting her daily activities. Based on the history of post-viral symptoms and exertional dyspnea, I need to evaluate for potential pulmonary hypertension or persistent inflammatory lung disease. I am requesting the results of the Chest X-Ray and BNP test we ordered to assess for fluid overload or structural lung abnormalities. If those results are inconclusive, we may need to consider further imaging or a trial of bronchodilators.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-infectious Bronchiolitis with Reactive Airway Dysfunction Syndrome (RADS) pending Chest_X-Ray and BNP results.
